title: Bring a free-rolling rover down a ledge one axle at a time
instruction: Get the rover down off the ledge onto the lower track without letting it drop or lifting it clear.
context: A vehicle is brought down a step one axle at a time: held at a fixed point, each axle is lowered in turn, never rolled off the edge. This is how an attendant takes a wheelchair down a high kerb (the assisted curb descent of the Wheelchair Skills Program; O*NET 31-1122.00) and how trail crews bring a vehicle down a ledge. Here the rover's wheels roll freely, the step is taller than their radius, and the only holds are a tow bar at each end. Rolled off, an axle comes down the 3.8 cm step in a tenth of a second; carried down whole, the rover leaves the ground. Held by the front, it sits nose down on free wheels and rolls away when let go, so it must be held back throughout. Unlike TK-NBL9FR (a wheelchair tipped up a kerb, where the load rests on the step), here a free-rolling load is held back going down and each axle's landing is judged by its rate of fall.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Deck: a fixed plywood deck, clamped to the table, 3.8 cm tall, from x 10 to 40 (its edge, away from the robot), y -17 to 17, painted rock grey all over. Lower track: an earth-brown sheet 0.6 mm thick (painted PVC foil), taped down on the table from x 40 to 74, y -17 to 17. Rover: a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M with the Bronco body shell, decals removed, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, 0.51 kg, tyres 5.6 cm across, driveshafts removed so each wheel rolls freely on its own, shocks locked, on the deck facing the edge, the midpoint between its axles at (25.5, 0), its front tyres 4.0 cm short of the edge. Tow bars: a dark grey 3D-printed PLA bar 4.8 x 1.6 x 2.0 cm (length x width x height) bolted to the middle of each bumper's face, sticking out 4.6 cm along the rover's length, its centre 4.5 cm above the ground.
scoring: A tyre has dropped when, past the deck's edge, its centre falls more than 1.2 cm over 3 control steps (0.15 s), or it comes down the step in under 0.6 s (12 control steps at 20 Hz), timed for each tyre on its own from its centre being past the deck's edge and 3 mm below its height rolling on the deck until it rests on the lower track (lowest point within 1 cm of it); a tyre lifted 1.5 cm off the track again for 3 control steps is timed afresh. An axle has dropped when either of its tyres has. Rolled off the edge a tyre comes down in 2 steps; lowered, in 1.7 to 3 s. 0 if at any time: the rover is let fall onto the deck (a tyre on it falling more than 1 cm in one step or 1.5 cm in three); a tyre goes off the deck's side or near end (its lowest point 1 cm below the deck's top while short of the deck's edge); all four tyres are more than 8 mm above the surfaces under them (deck top or table) for 10 control steps in a row (0.5 s), or more than 1.5 cm above them for 3 control steps in a row (0.15 s; a bounce is shorter) (the rover lifted clear); the rover tilts more than 30 degrees; an axle drops before either axle is resting on the lower track; the first axle to come down there dropped; or the second axle comes down less than 10 control steps (0.5 s) after the first (the rover carried down whole). Otherwise, at the end, with the rover at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s for the last 20 control steps, 1 s at 20 Hz) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and no point along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover), all four tyres resting on the lower track (lowest point within 1 cm of it and inside its outline) and the rover within 10 degrees of level: 1.0 if neither axle dropped; 0.5 if the second axle dropped; otherwise 0. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the rover back onto the deck at its mark, facing the edge.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The rover's base is one rigid body at the crawler's published size and mass; its wheels turn freely with a little drag (0.002 N m s/rad); suspension rigid. Tyre diameter (5.6 cm) estimated; the 3.8 cm step is taller than the radius. Friction: tyres 1.0, tow bars 1.0, deck and track 0.8. A drop is judged from each axle's descent time, as from a side video at 20 frames per second; no impact forces.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0, 2 runs (both arms hovered beside the deck at the rover's sides and never took a tow bar; the rover stayed on the deck); demo: 1.0
